subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish between lobopodium and filopodium. Give an example to each of them.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section, VSAQ chapter 16 'Locomotion & Reproduction' (book p.57, question 129). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely unrun; 'not checked' must never be read as 'checked and clean'. The mark split is this card's claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. MARKS: the VSAQ chapter header prints '2+2=4 MARKS', which is the blueprint's two 2-mark questions drawn from this unit, not 4 marks for one question; this card is authored at the Section A standard of 2 marks. APPEARANCES: the book prints [AP M-15,16,17] and [TS M-17,20] beside the two answer lines. TEXT BEYOND THE BOOK: the book gives one line per type; the lines saying a lobopodium carries both ectoplasm and endoplasm while a filopodium is ectoplasm alone are added here as standard zoology, because that is the structural difference behind the shapes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Lobopodium
lines: A lobopodium is a blunt, finger-like
It contains both ectoplasm and endoplasm.
steps.why: Both names describe a shape, so each answer line has to say the shape first; the example is then the mark the examiner can tick without reading further.
common_mistakes: Writing that a lobopodium is pointed. Its tip is blunt and rounded.
Giving no example. The question asks for one for each type.
steps.memory_tip: Lobe means a blunt rounded part, so a lobopodium is the blunt one.
steps.margin_note: Shape in one line, example in the next. Never leave the example out.

steps.label: Filopodium
lines: A filopodium is a long, fine, thread-like
It is made of ectoplasm only.
steps.why: A filopodium has no endoplasm inside it, and that is why it can stay so thin while a lobopodium has to stay thick.
common_mistakes: Writing Amoeba as the example for a filopodium. Amoeba forms lobopodia; Euglypha forms filopodia.
Calling a filopodium a network. A network of joined threads is a reticulopodium.
steps.memory_tip: Filo- means thread, as in filament: the thread-like one.
steps.margin_note: One mark each. The example is half of each mark.

insider_note: Every year some students write Amoeba for both types — the example is the fastest mark on this question and the easiest to lose.
